ak_main_boulders.blurb: A roadside cluster of boulders beside the Seward Highway, a short drive south of Anchorage, forming the main part of the Bird Creek bouldering. It holds 13 problems, from easy V1 slabs up through a solid block of V4s, with a handful of harder lines above V5 and one real test piece at the top end. The standout is a single large boulder with several quality lines, and a few more blocks lie scattered in the trees farther along the path. Walk-ins are almost nonexistent, so it suits a quick after-work session or a rest day, though highway noise is part of the deal. Sun and shade have not been well described, so expect to check it on the day.
ak_main_boulders.parking_note: Leave the car in the large Bird Creek lot off the Seward Highway south of Anchorage; the boulders are just beyond it.
ak_main_boulders.approach: Walk from the lot toward the creek, then turn up the slope on the left before the bridge. The main boulder is within a minute or two; more blocks are further along the trail in the forest.

ak_anchor_point_boulder.blurb: A lone granite erratic dropped by ice on the western Kenai Peninsula, north of Homer near the town of Anchor Point. Rock of this type is rare in the surrounding lowlands, which is what makes the block worth the trip. The 13 problems climb its southeast and southwest faces and span a wide range, from approachable V2 and V3 lines through the middle grades to several problems around V8 and V9 for strong boulderers. A tundra-covered back side gives an easy way down. It sees very little traffic, so bring pads, a partner, and a willingness to make a day of it with some brushy walking beside the river.

ak_diamond_the.blurb: The largest and best-known wall in the Archangel Valley at Hatcher Pass, north of Palmer. It has 13 routes, mostly traditional with three bolted lines, spread from moderate 5.7 terrain through a solid block of 5.9 and 5.10 up to a couple of 5.11 climbs. The granite is blocky and can grow moss when spring and fall are wet. Its south and north sides both carry lines, and the wall offers longer outings than most crags in the valley, including a multi-pitch classic. Approaches are fairly short by alpine standards, though the dirt road in can demand a high-clearance vehicle, so plan your drive.

ak_zulu_wall.blurb: A mixed-bag wall in the Archangel Valley at Hatcher Pass, north of Palmer. Its 13 routes include mostly trad lines plus a few bolted ones, covering nearly the whole range from 5.6 and 5.7 starters through plenty of 5.9 and 5.10, with a single 5.11 and a lone 5.12 for the strong. Styles vary, and stemming along vertical dikes is part of the character, so it suits a party with mixed abilities who want variety in one place. The granite is blocky and tends to collect moss when spring and fall are rainy.

ak_wishbone.blurb: A small, sunny wall high in the Archangel Valley at Hatcher Pass, part of the Fairangel Walls and sitting above the trail toward Fairangel Gap. It holds 13 routes of mixed style, with trad lines in the majority, some bolted leads and one top-rope, graded from 5.7 up to 5.12. Grades cluster around 5.10, with a few easier lines for warming up and a couple of hard sport and crack pitches for the keen. Routes are short, so expect single-pitch days rather than long outings, and some older protection may need a careful look. It is a handy stop for a party wanting a moderate-to-hard tick list in the south-facing sun.
ak_wishbone.approach: From the outhouse, follow the road a short way toward the mine gate, then take the hikers' trail across the creek and climb the slope to the base of the wall.
